caption: The drawing is composed of a central image featuring a horse and a rider. Both the horse and the rider are depicted in shades of brown and tan, with intricate linework creating a braided, rope-like texture over their bodies. The horse is standing in profile facing left, with its mane and tail rendered as multiple strands suggesting hair or fibers. The rider sits upright on the horse's back and is clothed in a long, cylindrical skirt or garment with a hood or pointed hat that covers the head. The outlines and details of the horse and rider are made up of repeated, rounded segments that resemble coils or braided ropes. The drawing is centered within a rectangular border on a cream-colored background, with ample negative space surrounding the figures. The artist's name, Wilbur M. Rice, is written in small text at the bottom right corner of the image.
title: Corn Husk Doll on Horse
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
